# The Glass Thorn

*Pages PDF 83-90*

## **The Glass Thorn**
## **A Secret War**
The Druchii may regard the other species of the world as little more than vermin, but even these contemptible creatures could prove a threat to the Dread King’s plans, so he sends forth spies and saboteurs to keep him informed of the plans of his enemies and act early to frustrate them. Given the paranoia intrinsic to dark elf society, Malerion is not the only important dark elf to employ spies, so the agents of many highborn houses or covens of sorceresses are sent abroad. One of the most established spy rings is the Glass Thorn, whose agents report to the experienced spymaster Harzeth Duskmantle. 

## **The Legend of the Glass Thorn**
When the high elves made war with dwarfs in elthin arvan, Malerion took the chance to strike at Ulthuan and the Dread King fought many battles against his hated kin. During one engagement, he beheaded a Caledorian prince, whose mount, the dragon Voruthir, flew at the Dread King in a rage. The battle lasted many days before Malerion struck an enchanted crystal dagger into the dragon’s skull. The beast escaped, but all the while the glass thorn penetrated deeper into its brain. as it limped back to Caledor, insanity seized Voruthir, and the great beast incinerated many high elves before dying in agony. 

The Glass Thorn is composed of Druchii agents deployed under cover amongst humans and elves in the northern Empire and Bretonnia, spying for Anethra Helbane. They are not the only Druchii spy ring in the region, as spies in service of Clar Karond compete with them for information and leverage for their masters back in Naggaroth. 

Spymaster Harzeth Duskmantle gives his agents freedom to act as they choose, providing they produce useful intelligence, complete their assignments, and continue to conceal the existence of the Glass Thorn. He keeps their identities secret from each other, lest they conspire against him or jeopardise the integrity of the spy ring. Nevertheless, various agents are in contact, sending coded missives and meeting in person in remote ruins or the secluded corners of cities. They are a diverse group, united in their hatred of high elves and a desire to undermine the power of Old World nations. All are steeped in the pervasive paranoia of dark elf culture, which is excellent training for the constant vigilance of a spy’s life. Some agents control their own dark elf spies, while others recruit human dupes to do their work. A handful are lone wolves, trusting no one’s competence or loyalty. 

The Glass Thorn is an effective spy ring, though Duskmantle lacks the numbers or resources to bring true devastation to Clar Karond’s enemies. This could easily change if they worked in concert with other forces on _Temple of Spite_ . 

## **Goals**
The Glass Thorn advances the cause of the Helbanes, Clar Karond, and Malerion through espionage, sabotage, and assassination. 

Glass Thorn agents assassinate and terrorise high elves, leaving unambiguous messages to demonstrate the long reach of Malerion. 

**Uncover Empire and Bretonnian secrets.** Agents gather intelligence on the Empire and Bretonnia’s military ambitions, particularly their naval strength, defensive capabilities, and overseas ventures. Myrentha Selkarth reports on the Empire’s shoreline defences and spies on shipyards. Daleathra Bladeborn keeps a close watch on the Colleges of Magic and human attempts to master magic, including those who pursue necromancy or daemonology, all of which could threaten Druchii ambitions. 

**Weaken alliances** . Instability serves Naggaroth’s interests, so the Glass Thorn’s agents look for cracks in their enemies’ cohesion and strive to lever them open. Several political and mercantile rivalries in Marienburg have intensified through Duskmantle’s efforts, ensuring purloined documents appear on the wrong desk, or that cargo ships follow false charts. Clashes between the Eonir and human foresters were catalysed by Khoruan Liereth’s agents, to drive a wedge in human-elf relations. 

**Counter elven espionage.** The Glass Thorn fights a secret war against Ulthuan’s spies and envoys, particularly those from Lothern and Saphery. Each side plays a game of cat and mouse, seeking to uncover, frustrate, and eliminate the other. 

**Monitor the advance of Chaos.** Human Chaos worshippers and gullible Norscans are useful pawns, but dark elves are wary of the consequences should the Ruinous Powers seize control of humanity. Agents, particularly Sylthir Ashrend and Ryna Morbeth, investigate cults and track beastman and marauder raids. More than one witch hunter has received surreptitious aid from the Glass Thorn, though they would never guess the identity of their mysterious allies. 

**Escape detection.** Agents’ identities and the operations of the Glass Thorn must remain secret, and so all cover their tracks and eliminate those who know too much. Should an agent jeopardise the spy ring’s security, they soon find a dagger in their back. 

**Inflict harm** . Most sabotage operations are intended to advance Druchii goals, yet sometimes cruelty is enough. A poisoned well, a sunken ship, an inn torched with all inside — for the Druchii, watching Old Worlders suffer can be an end in itself. 

**Betrayal** . Each spy is loyal while it suits and ambitious to rise in the hierarchy. All agents look for opportunities for advantage over one another, providing they can keep evidence of their perfidy hidden.

## **In the Old World**
The Glass Thorn consists of at least 12 Druchii agents controlled by spymaster Huriel Duskmantle from Marienburg. The majority live in cities in the Empire and Bretonnia, where elves are a common sight. While all agents travel on assignments, some are permanent wanderers, moving continuously to fulfil their mission. 

## **Relations with** _**Temple of Spite**_
When _Temple of Spite_ is close to Marienburg, Harzeth Duskmantle absconds under cover of night by ravenship and ascends discretely to the Chain Spire to meet Duriath Helbane in person. No other agents have seen the ark’s towers since disembarking onto the shores of the Old World, they are dedicated to their roles and do not expect to return. 

The Glass Thorn is a significant asset for Duriath Helbane. Anethra directed Harzeth to liaise with the fleetmaster, which provides Duriath with valuable intelligence and influence back in Clar Karond. It is a tool to harm his rivals, particularly the Fellhearts of Karond Kar. Helbane has a personal relationship with Duskmantle and never allows intermediaries to come between them. Providing the spymaster follows orders and produces results, Helbane treats him with respect. 

Unknown to Helbane, Malerion’s envoy Myrrhven Silkblood also commands the Glass Thorn, on behalf of the Dread King. As Duskmantle serves two masters, he is careful to keep Silkblood’s requests and intelligence hidden from the fleetmaster, for he fears Malerion’s wrath more than Clar Karond’s. 

While Glass Thorn spies are competent killers, Harzeth prefers to use Khainite assassins to eliminate important targets, to reduce the risk of his agents coming under suspicion. Death Hag Kheitalla accedes to his requests as they serve to remind everyone of the far reach and infallibility of Khainite assassins. 

Few inhabitants of _Temple of Spite_ know anything of the Glass Thorn, but Khaines’ Eyes are an exception. The shades and dark riders occasionally liaise with agents to exchange information or cooperate in acts of violence. There is little trust between them, particularly as Duskmantle sees Samuril’s network of human agents as infringing on his domain. 

introduction from Anethra Helbane, complete with her magical seal. Duskmantle despatched him to L’Anguille, where he feigns allegiance to the Glass Thorn, while striving to identify his fellow agents, pass intelligence to Sapherian spies in Altdorf, and minimise harm from dark elf schemes. 

The ring of human agents working for Sylthin Ashrend in Carroburg intend to murder him for his gold. Delaethra Bladeborn discovered the plot and is debating whether to intervene and put Ashrend in her debt, or let it happen and take control of Carroburg herself. 

The sorceress Ucelia Erevien works with two agents from Clar Karond in Salzenmund. She is more interested in a fragment of a black ark that is located in the city than any rivalry with other spy rings. Her intelligence has declined in quality, and Duskmantle wants to know why. 

## **But I Hate Them…**
Dark elf spies hate high elves, but they would not stay hidden long if they revert to blind violence on sight. They learn to mask their loathing behind their cover identity. When creating dark elf spies, remove the _Hatred (High Elves)_ Talent/Trait from their profile. 

## **Meeting Glass Thorn Agents**
Dealing with the Glass Thorn means dealing with their schemes and machinations, as direct conflict will require investigation first. Characters could become aware of crimes involving stolen documents or sabotaged ships, then follow a well-concealed trail to a seemingly-innocent elf. Perhaps a prominent figure is blackmailed, ruined, or assassinated, and the Characters are hired to investigate. 

The Glass Thorn often acts through unknowing pawns. Wherever there is clandestine work to be done, hapless Characters could be hired to unknowingly advance _Temple of Spite’s_ interests. Dark elves delight in using deception and persuasion, so an agent might offer idealistic parties an opportunity to help a cause that matters to them. Patriotic Characters are told their mission counters enemies of the state, while other Characters might simply appreciate a large payout from a wealthy elf. 

## **Internal Tensions**
‘Graelis Doomveil’ is a high elf double agent. Two years ago, Eryndor Brightmere voyaged from Saphery to Marienburg and presented Harzeth Duskmantle with a forged letter of 

An agent may help the party out of a predicament, such as rescuing them from the law, goblins, or another misfortune. Of course, they will want favours in return for such assistance. 

## **Exactly as Planned — Easy Encounter**
The Salkalten docks are quiet tonight, lit only by a few lanterns swaying in the breeze. Dockside thugs in the pay of Khardil Ulakth are creeping towards _Beloved of Tralinia_ , an elven trade ship berthed overnight as it makes its way to Erengrad. Ulakth stays in the _Siren’s Crown_ inn, using Night Vision to watch as a band of dockside thugs begin to cut down the ship’s rigging and drill holes in her hull below the waterline. They don’t realise they’re a distraction, and that while they make noise and attract the attention of the sea elf crew, Ulakth slips out to inscribe a cursed rune onto the prow, which will ignite once the ship is at sea. 

The party easily notice four humans attempting to damage _Beloved of Tralinia_ . If they intervene, the thugs fight and, in defeat, reveal they were hired by an elf in the Siren’s Crown. 

Ulakth does not hide. After all, people in Salkalten know him as a sea elf. He simply explains that he was testing the guard on the ship. Nobody would seriously think the thugs’ pathetic _try_ to tools could damage an elven ship. The Characters could persuade the _Beloved of Tralinia’s_ crew that a fellow sea elf wants to sink their ship. If the party appears competent, Ulakth may hire them for a job.

## **Missing at Midnight — Hard Encounter**
Carroburg’s underworld has a new kingpin, and now, whenever they threaten the Carver Boys, rival gangs simply disappear. Once they ran a few alleyways around Polldamer Strasse, now they have half the city. The new boss is Sylthir Ashrend, who instructs the Carver Boys to capture their enemies, load them onto barges with other unfortunates, and sail downstream. Under cover of darkness, they liaise with _Hunter’s Spear_ , a wrackhold ship anchored in a Reik tributary. The captives are taken north to the open sea and _Temple of Spite_ . 

The party could meet the barges or _Hunter’s Spear_ on the river, or could themselves fall foul of the Carver Boys in Carroburg. The players might catch sight of a barge being loaded in moonlight by half-seen figures herding frightened prisoners aboard. _Hunter’s Spear_ flies the colours of Marienburg and sails only at night. If the Characters come to a fight, they have a major battle on their hands. 

- Nalith Soultearer (Dark Elf Highborn Officer) 

## **The Couronne Connection — Medium Encounter**
A high elf body was found on the steps of the temple of Shallya in Couronne, his throat and wrists cut to the bone. The Matriarche of Shallya and the city’s bailiff are outraged, especially as the city is full of pilgrims visiting Shallya’s holy waters. Ithalan Moondawn was an Eataine spy who compiled a list of dark elf agents in Bretonnia and the Reikland. Nyxar Vorn found out and summoned an assassin from _Temple of Spite_ to kill Moondawn, who had secured the papers elsewhere.

## **‘Huriel Greybreeze’ (Harzeth Duskmantle), Dark Elf Spymaster**
Huriel Greybreeze lives in a modest house on the island of Vlothuis in Elfsgemeente, Marienburg. His study is piled high with scrolls and tomes, research into the lost elven colonies of the Old World. He enjoys discussing such matters with intelligent enquirers and sells manuscripts he no longer needs. Greybreeze is considerate and unassuming, perhaps a little disorganised.

## **Armour**
He wears typical sea elf robes and an owlish, slightly melancholy expression, but this cover identity hides an elf mired in a secret war with multiple fronts. He works against the Exarchate and the Ten in Marienburg, but mostly he coordinates the Glass Thorn. Duskmantle walks a tightrope between rival masters, Helbane and Malerion, whose agendas pull in different directions: each demanding loyalty, each prepared to discard him should he falter. 

Duskmantle liaises with agents outside Marienburg under the pretence of travelling to ancient elven sites. He reports back to _Temple of Spite_ by feeding a coded message to an ensorcelled seagull, which flies to the ark, where only Duriath Helbane is permitted to slice open the bird to receive Duskmantle’s report.

## **A Silken Web**
harzeth Duskmantle has built a network of informants in the major elven households in Marienburg. These are human servants who believe they are working for the Directorate as a check on elven power in the city. Duskmantle works through Marijke Jansen, a laundress who arranges to meet the informants by placing silk handkerchiefs when returning their household laundry. These are embroidered with a coded pattern indicating the time and place for the liaison. The Characters witness as Jansen is pickpocketed.  she begs the Characters to help her recover her handkerchiefs and seems disproportionately upset. If they return the handkerchiefs, Jansen breaks down and begs for help to escape harzeth’s control. They must be discreet, as the spymaster has threatened her family. 

## **‘Thalania Dawnspear’ (Selin Ebonspite), Dark Elf Agent**
Selin Ebonspite is a true daughter of Naggaroth, cold as the land of her birth. She ghosts through the Grey Mountain foothills, scouring secret places for knowledge and her enemies’ weaknesses. Every movement is measured, every word weighed, and even her silence is purposeful. 

Ebonspite mostly avoids company, and those who meet ‘Thalania’ encounter a wood elf remarkable for her stillness and silver-eyed gaze. Clad in the greens and greys of the Asrai, she poses as a waywatcher, a quiet warden of the glades scouting for threats to Athel Loren. 

She stays on the move, crossing the Grey Mountains to spy on Athel Loren and human lands on both sides of the mountains. She seeks out border disputes or ambitious nobles, which she reports back to Duskmantle. If a high elf ventures close, she eagerly plots their death. Ebonspite is not averse to passing intelligence to the Asrai in Arranoc, as it helps protect her cover and she holds no particular animus for the wood elves.

## **Stirring the Pot**
a spate of murders on the outskirts of the Wissenland villages of owingen and heisenberg have caused disquiet amongst the burghers of Meissen. Pedlars and mountain men are found dead, pin-cushioned with crossbow bolts of unmistakable dwarfen manufacture. nothing connects the victims, the deaths seem indiscriminate. locals grumble that the dwarfs of Karak norn are showing their true colours. selin ebonspite has a plentiful supply of bolts and intends to stay in the area a while longer, to see whether she can inspire open conflict. 

## **‘Pethia Starwhisper’ (Dalaethra Bladeborn), Dark Elf Agent**
Simply everybody in Altdorf high society is talking about Pethia’s marvellous parties. She may be a high elf, but she’s not superior like the rest of them, and Pethia’s flamboyance, sharp wit, and social agility bring an eclectic crowd of artists, nobles, sea lords, generals, wizards, and oddballs into an atmosphere of irreverent, effusive gossip. It is no secret that most guests soon come to harbour affections for Pethia. Her vivacious looks and devastating smile carry a hint of mischief that is hard to resist. 

Dalaethra is a socialite and a devoted follower of Khaine, and if that sounds like a contradiction, it is. Disguised as a Cothiqui merchant, she manipulates her admirers into giving up secrets, promising, but never delivering, romance. Should they fail, they see her other side and serve her out of fear. Dalaethra’s sources include an Imperial engineer, magisters from the Celestial and Gold Colleges, several functionaries in the Imperial court, a senior priest of Sigmar, and a Sapherian emissary. 

Life in Altdorf suits Dalaethra. When the last guests leave the party, she slips out into the night to pay homage to her bloodyhanded god. In a city like Altdorf, with so many people, the deaths are barely noticed by anyone other than her lord Khaine.

## **The Snub**
Bors von Heedon was delighted when he finally secured an invitation to one of Pethia starwhisper’s gatherings. he’d finally arrived on Altdorf’s social scene and intended to make an impression on everyone present. The evening did not go as planned. his hunting anecdotes were met with glazed looks, and when starwhisper mocked his green cross-garters and limp ruff, he stormed out in humiliation. he is bent on revenge and hires the Characters to uncover anything that might cause starwhisper similar embarrassment. 

## **Perfidious Naggaroth**
_‘I can see you are wise, your majesty. You know the softest voices carry the sharpest truths. Lend me your ear, and I shall lend you an advantage.’_ — Vaelia Whitepyre, Envoy to the Court of Bilbali 

The Sultan of Copher occasionally consults the humble Lordling Mordelain, whose contacts in Bilbali and Magritta seem exceptionally well-informed. 

## **Grand Cathay**
Elves manipulate other species wherever they find them. The Asur argue this is for the greater good, and that lesser creatures need guidance to keep the forces of darkness at bay. The Druchii have no such delusions — they manipulate to dominate. It is their destiny to rule the world by might and deception. Diplomacy plays its part, as there are few more satisfying sights than watching allies die on the field of battle in service to a Druchii agenda. Silver-tongued emissaries are found in the most unlikely places, negotiating arrangements of mutual benefit and casting suspicion on their high elf counterparts. 

Beyond the activities of the Glass Thorn, the Black Convocation strives to bend other species to their will. 

## **Norscans**
The reckless Norse are notorious for raiding Ulthuan and they are often the harbingers of a larger Chaos incursion. Helbane sent a tough envoy, Kaelith Ironshard, with an entourage of bleakswords to monitor and influence Bjornling, Graeling, and Skaeling jarls. If weasel words don’t work, Helbane is considering threatening any reluctant jarls with the revealed might of his black ark. 

Fu-Chow hosts a population of elves from all of Ulthuan’s kingdoms, where they vie for good relations with Yin-Yin, Mistress of the Jade Sea and ruler of the eastern kingdoms. The brothers Jahien and Traquael Hexbrand claim to originate from Arnheim and run a trading concern dealing in tea and spices. Their real business is scrutinising Asur activity and spreading disinformation about the politics of Grand Cathay. 

## **Madness in Myrmidens**
Citizens whisper of a sudden madness stalking Myrmidens’ halls of power. senators of the border princedom make puzzling decisions, leading to broken alliances, trade routes abandoned, and military orders almost designed to fail. The source is an enigmatic elven envoy with gentle words. Her influence seems benign, until those who threaten to restore sanity vanish or turn on one another. 

halkia syrillin weaves madness into the fabric of the city. she hopes to rule Myrmidens in the name of Karond Kar and may well succeed unless Captain redthorn from _Temple of Spite_ can fulfil her assignment to thwart her efforts. The party would make ideal sacrificial assets to spearhead an attempt to displace syrillin from Myrmidens. 

## **Orcs, Goblins, and Related Species**
Goblins and orcs are so single-minded that manipulation is surprisingly difficult. Hobgoblins are a little different, as dark elves occasionally use them as mercenaries. Twenty years ago, _Temple of Spite_ carried Lord Khron Nightglade of Clar Karond to make an overland trek into the vast steppes north of Mountains of Mourn to visit the Hobgobla Khan’s nomadic court. He remains a guest of the hobgoblins to this day. 

## **Undead**
Life amongst the tomb kings is unbearably dull and (literally) bloodless for a dark elf, and spies with flesh on them tend to stand out. Captain Filvanir attempted to trade with Zandri, to no avail. In contrast, the Vampire Coast is surprisingly amenable to dark elf alliance (see page 75). 

## **Estalia and Araby**
_Temple of Spite_ has advisers embedded in Estalian and Arabyan courts. Sorceress Yrleth has the ear of Queen Juana la Roja of Bilbali, thanks to secrets she shares from spies in Magritta and Copher. Lady Ganethia advises the Lords of Magritta in matters political, military, and mercantile, providing intelligence from Copher and Bilbali to gain favour.
